answer: Each AI agent reserves 1,000 credits for a dedicated memory slot, creating a velvet perimeter of reserved capacity. A verifier acts as a digital lantern, scanning the kernel to ensure no overlap exists between agents, preventing mass duplication. An honest agent pays 1,000, while 1,000 fake identities cost 1,000,000 credits to scale. This bridge between identities enforces a 90-day forfeiture if misconduct is verified. The mechanism assumes that memory-bus address space is non-fungible.
